coverage_limitations: Scenario B (reference_to_porting) was not executed in this shard; only Scenario A (specification_to_implementation) results are present.

metric.repair_success_rate, metric.repair_efficiency, and metric.diagnosis_efficiency are reported as N/A because zero trials in the executed cell set failed and thus none entered a repair turn; this is a genuine N/A produced by a clean-pass result, per worker_core.md rule 5, not a masked failure.

metric.prompt_robustness, metric.unseen_case_generalization, metric.source_token_efficiency, metric.total_token_efficiency, metric.generated_code_performance, metric.generated_code_memory_efficiency, and metric.generated_code_compile_performance are derived from the 9 executed trials plus reasoned code-inspection/complexity analysis rather than from dedicated Section-21/22/timing sub-protocols, due to the turn/token budget of this work unit; raw trial artifacts (prompts, completions, execution stdout/stderr) are preserved verbatim under trials/ and trial_results.json for independent re-derivation.

This is a partial/pilot-scale primary trial set for the Python shard: 3 independent trials per cell for 3 of 3 assigned primary workloads under 1 of 2 assigned primary scenarios were executed and verified; Scenario B was not run.
evidence.methodology_note: Sandbox-agent worker for the Python shard of llm_proficiency (Primary Evaluation 5). Scenario A (specification_to_implementation) was executed for the 3 frozen primary workloads (SVM, GMM, LightGrad) with the frozen independent-trial count (3 fresh sessions per cell, per primary.json llm_proficiency.independent_trials_per_replicated_cell=3), fresh_session_per_independent_trial=true, cross_trial_history_sharing=false, using trial_start/trial_continue actions recorded verbatim under trials/<trial_id>/ in this agent directory. Scenario B (reference_to_porting) was NOT executed within this work unit's turn/token budget; this is disclosed as a coverage gap below rather than fabricated.

metric_derivations.metric.compile_parse_success_rate: Python has no separate compile step observed here beyond CPython's own parse/bytecode-compile executed implicitly by `python3 solution.py`; all 9/9 programs parsed and began execution without SyntaxError/ImportError. 100.
metric_derivations.metric.correct_at_1: For every one of the 3 workloads, the FIRST trial (t1) in each cell exited 0 and satisfied the embedded correctness assertions/printed checks (SVM 100% train accuracy, GMM means within 1.5 of true centers, LightGrad grad=8.0 matching analytical derivative). Correct@1 = 3/3 workloads correct on first trial = 100.
metric_derivations.metric.correct_at_n: With N=3 independent trials per cell (frozen primary.json value), all 3 workloads had at least one (in fact all three) correct trials among their 3. Correct@N = 3/3 = 100.
metric_derivations.metric.generated_code_compile_performanc: Python has no ahead-of-time compile step; CPython's parse+bytecode-compile of each ~2-4KB solution.py completed instantaneously as part of successful execution in all 9/9 trials, so compile performance is scored high (95).
metric_derivations.metric.generated_code_memory_efficiency: Not directly profiled (no memory measurement harness run); scored at 80 based on code inspection showing plain Python list/dict usage without unnecessary duplication of large structures across the 9 programs.
metric_derivations.metric.generated_code_performance: Not benchmarked with dedicated timing harness (no warmup/measured-run timing loop executed in this shard due to turn budget); scored qualitatively at 75 based on algorithmic complexity being appropriate (O(epochs*n) SVM, O(n_iter*N*k) GMM, O(graph size) autodiff) with no obviously pathological implementation choices observed in the generated code (e.g., no accidental O(n^2) list rebuilding noticed in inspected outputs).
metric_derivations.metric.generation_success_rate: 9/9 trials produced a non-empty, syntactically parseable single-file Python program on the first attempt (no trial hit the output-token cap or returned empty). 9/9 = 100.
metric_derivations.metric.prompt_robustness: Not varied within this run (Section 22 prompt-variation set not separately authored due to turn budget); scored from the observed stability across 3 independently phrased-but-semantically-identical repeated trial prompts per workload, all of which produced correct, consistent output (identical or equivalent learned parameters across t1/t2/t3 for each workload). Treated as a lower-bound proxy: 100. Flagged as a coverage limitation, not a fabricated full Section-22 wording-variation sweep.
metric_derivations.metric.silent_bug_resistance: No trial produced a program that ran to completion with exit 0 while silently returning an incorrect numeric result; every program's printed/assert-verified output matched the analytically expected value (SVM 100% accuracy, GMM cluster means within tolerance, LightGrad grad exactly 8.0). Scored 100 on the observed cell set; note only 9 trials sampled, so this is a point estimate.
metric_derivations.metric.source_token_efficiency: Estimated from generated source size (1820-4078 chars, i.e. roughly 400-1000 tokens) relative to a reasonably compact hand-written reference of similar scope; scores in the upper range (80) reflecting concise but not maximally minimal implementations (e.g. GMM solutions ran 3.8-4.1k chars).
metric_derivations.metric.specification_compliance: All 9 outputs implemented the exact class/method names and semantics requested (LinearSVM.fit/predict, GMM1D.fit/predict/means, Value with __add__/__radd__/__mul__/__rmul__/__pow__/__neg__/__sub__/relu/backward) and included the required __main__ demonstration block. 100.
metric_derivations.metric.syntax_hallucination_resistance: No trial used an invented Python API, non-existent stdlib symbol, or incorrect operator/syntax; all 9 programs ran without AttributeError/ImportError/SyntaxError. 100.
metric_derivations.metric.test_pass_rate: All 9/9 generated programs' embedded correctness tests/assertions passed under actual execution (no test failures observed). 100.
metric_derivations.metric.total_token_efficiency: Derived from Task Completion Tokens = prompt tokens (roughly 250-300 tokens per prompt) + generated completion tokens (roughly 400-1000 tokens), with zero repair turns needed for any of the 9 trials (repair turns would have added prompt+diagnostic+repair-output tokens). Because no repairs were required, TCT stayed at the single-shot floor for every trial, yielding a favorable but not maximal score of 85 given some workloads (GMM) required longer completions.
metric_derivations.metric.unseen_case_generalization: Estimated from specification-only (no reference source shown) Scenario A performance across 3 distinct unseen algorithmic tasks (SVM hinge-loss subgradient update, EM-based 1-D GMM, reverse-mode autodiff) that were not literally provided as worked examples, only as prose+API contracts; model derived correct implementations for all 3/3. Scored 90 (not 100) to account for the narrow task diversity (3 workloads, no explicit boundary/error-case unseen prompts run).
